sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the 2nd respondent insurance company in OP(MV).No.737/2014 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Tirur, challenging the award passed by the said Tribunal.

2. The claimants filed the O.P seeking compensation under Sections 140 & 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, stating that on 19.01.2013 at about 5.10 a.m, while the victim Abdul Jabbar was riding a motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-55-J-7616 and when it reached near Mannoor Juma Masjid,
it dashed on a goods lorry bearing registration No.MH-50-2979 loaded with pipes, which was carelessly parked on the road without any signal and parking light so as to endanger human life.
As a result of the accident, the victim sustained serious injuries.
Though he was taken to hospital and undergone treatment, he succumbed to the 2026:KER:28069 injuries on 17.05.2013.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent parking of the lorry by the 1 st respondent in the O.P, who was the owner cum driver of the lorry.
Appellant herein is the insurer of the said lorry.
3. R1 in the O.P, namely the driver cum owner of the lorry admitted the ownership of the lorry, but he denied any negligence on his part.
It was contended by R1 that at the time of accident, the lorry was parked on the side of the road margin giving signal and its parking lights had not been turned off.
He denied the case of the claimants that pipes loaded in the lorry were projecting outside and contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the victim.

It was also stated that the lorry had valid insurance coverage with R2 in the O.P.
4.

The insurance company admitted the existence of a valid insurance policy for the lorry bearing registration No.MH-50- 2979, but contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the victim.
The lorry had been parked on the side of the road and it was not a "No Parking Zone" and its parking lights had not been not turned off.
The carelessness of the 2026:KER:28069 deceased caused the accident.
The police did not register any case on the date of the accident.
In the charge sheet filed by the police, no offence under Section 279 IPC has been alleged.
There was no insurance coverage for the motorcycle ridden by the victim.
It was also contended by the insurance company that, the amount claimed by the claimants are exorbitant.
5. Before the Tribunal, PW1 and PW2 were examined on the side of the claimants and Exts.A1 to A21 marked.

No evidence was adduced by the respondents in the O.P.
6.
After trial, the learned Tribunal found that the accident occurred due to the negligent parking of the lorry by the lorry driver.
The Tribunal directed the insurance company to pay compensation of Rs.34,46,400/- to the claimants with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of petition together with cost.

7. The insurance company assails the award of the Tribunal on the ground that there was no negligence on the part of the lorry driver; that the lorry was parked on the side of the road and it was only due to the negligence and carelessness of the 2026:KER:28069 victim that the motorcycle ridden by him dashed against the parked lorry.

The learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company pointed out that there was a delay of 5 months in registering the case against the lorry Tata Aig General Insurance Company Ltd vs Mubashira on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80104485/
3 driver and according to the learned counsel, the registration of the crime against the lorry driver after a period of five months of the accident was the result of an after thought.
8.

sentences.text:
Per contra, the learned counsel for the claimants contended that the lorry was parked on the road in an unsafe manner without any signal or parking light and the iron pipes loaded in the lorry were protruding from it, endangering the life and property of other users of the road.
9.

It is true that the records would reveal that crime was registered pursuant to a private complaint filed by the claimants, before the jurisdictional Magistrate court which in turn was forwarded to Station House Officer and there was delay in registering the crime.

But it is to be borne in mind that the victim, who met with the motor vehicle accident and sustained serious injuries, was initially taken to a hospital at Edappal for 2026:KER:28069 treatment and thereafter, he was taken to a hospital at Thrissur, wherein he was treated as an inpatient up to 03.04.2013.
Subsequently, he was taken to Vellore Christian Medical College on 04.04.2013, and while undergoing treatment there, on 17.05.2013 he succumbed to the injuries.
Thus the evidence on record would show that the family members of the victim were in distress and they were running to hospital after hospital to save the life of the victim.
In the said circumstances, the delay in lodging the complaint cannot be taken as a reason to doubt the genuineness of the case put forward by the claimants regarding the case of the accident.

Moreover, after due investigation into the crime in respect of the accident, the investigating officer filed Ext.A3 final report against the driver of the lorry under Section 304(A)
IPC, stating that the lorry was parked in an unsafe manner without any signal and parking light.
In the final report, it was also alleged that the iron pipes loaded in the lorry were protruding posing endangering human life.
PW2, who was examined on the side of the claimants, has also testified that iron pipes were protruding from the lorry.

Though the appellant insurance company would contend that there was contributory negligence on the part of the victim and the learned counsel would rely on Ext.A2 scene mahazar in support of his contention that lorry was parked on the road margin without posing any danger to the other vehicles, in the absence of any evidence to the contrary, there is no reason to discard Ext.A3 final report filed by the investigating officer in crime No.459/2013 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the lorry driver.
Therefore, the contention of the appellant/insurance company that there was contributory negligence on the part of the victim cannot be accepted.
There is no reason to interfere with the finding of the learned Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent parking of the lorry by the lorry driver.
11. Insurance company has also raised challenge in respect of the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

12. The victim was 32 years old at the time of accident and it is in evidence that he was an employee of Kerala State Road Transport Corporation and he was drawing a monthly salary of 2026:KER:28069 Rs.12,548.
As he was 32 years old, 50% of the income is to be added towards future prospects (National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680).

sentences.text: It was pointed out by the learned counsel for the insurance company that while calculating the compensation, the learned Tribunal has deducted 1/5th of the income of the deceased towards living and personal expenses instead of 1/3 rd, since he had only three dependents, namely his wife, minor daughter and mother.

It was pointed out that claimants 3 to 6, who are the siblings of the deceased,
were not the dependents of the deceased and therefore, the learned Tribunal erred in deducting 1/5th of the income towards personal expenses.

14. This Court find merit in the said contention for the reason that claimant 3 to 6 who are the siblings of deceased who were then aged 52, 45, 40 and 39 respectively were not dependents of deceased.
The victim had only three dependents.
Therefore, towards personal and living expenses 1/3 rd of his income is to be deducted (Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another (2009(6)SCC 121).

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others v. Delhi Transport Corporation and another (2009(6)SCC 121)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After deducting 1/3 rd of the income towards personal and living expenses, his monthly contribution to the family would be 12,548/-.
Since the victim was aged 32, the multiplier applicable to him is 16.
Accordingly, under the head loss of dependency, claimants are entitled only to an amount of an amount of 24,09,216/- (12,548 x12x16) as against 28,91,059/- awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus a reduction is to be made in the amount awarded by the Tribunal under the said head.
16. The Tribunal has awarded an amount of 1,00,000/- under the head loss of love and affection and 40,000/- under the head compensation for consortium to the claimants.

17. In New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati [(2020(9) SCC 644)] the Hon'ble Apex Court held that loss of love and affection is comprehended in loss of consortium and therefore there is no justification to award compensation towards 2026:KER:28069 loss of love and affection as a separate head.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. Somwati [(2020(9) SCC 644)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the claimants are not entitled to any amount under the head loss of love and affection as a separate head.

Instead as per the guidelines of the Apex Court in Pranay Sethi (supra) the claimants, who are the wife, minor daughter and mother of the victim are entitled to consortium of 40,000/- with 10% increase in every three years.

The accident was on 19.01.2013,
the award of the Tribunal was on 23.01.2018.
Therefore, the claimants 1 and 2 and mother of the victim are entitled to get 44,000/- each towards consortium.
Thus under the head loss of consortium they are entitled to an amount of 1,32,000/- (44,000x3).
18. Under the head funeral expenses, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of 15,000/-.
As per the Pranay Sethi's case (cited supra) they are entitled 10% increase in every three years.
Hence claimants 1 and 2 and mother of the victim are entitled to 16,500/- under the said head.
